title: The Kettlebell Code (second edition)
note: A short training e-book aimed at people over 40. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A kettlebell coach’s case that people over 40 should train with a few versatile movements rather than machines, and his three-part method for doing it. The first part restores mobility and movement patterns (hinge, squat, overhead) with stick drills and light work. The second builds strength with the slow “grinds” (presses, squats, lunges) and power with the ballistic lifts (swings, cleans, snatches), plus loaded carries. The third assembles these into short sessions with warm-ups and recommended weights. A personal prologue and epilogue frame the method as a way of taking charge of one’s health.

chapters.title: Prologue: The Mezzanine of Destiny
chapters.summary: A personal story of a career crisis that led the author to kettlebells, and the argument for short, home-based training over gym machines after 40.

chapters.title: Part I: Loosen Your Body’s Brakes
chapters.summary: Mobility first: drills with a stick and light weights to open the hips, shoulders and spine and learn the basic patterns.

chapters.title: Part II: Turn Force into Form
chapters.summary: The main lifts: grinds (press, goblet squat, reverse lunge), ballistics (swing variants, clean, snatch), and carries.

chapters.title: Part III: Unlock the Code
chapters.summary: Putting it together into sessions: warm-up, activation, main work and finisher, with weights by level.

chapters.title: Epilogue and appendix
chapters.summary: What the book left out (double-bell work and more), encouragement to keep going, and the reference list.
